newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.
newsitem.headline: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.

text.p: Vacant primary elevator space remained unchanged in the past week as railcar unloads at export ports fell below target, Canadian Wheat Board said.
Average vacancy in Prairie elevators was 18 percent in the week ended March 16, unchanged from the week before, CWB said.
Weather and equipment failure caused delays in shipping grains and oilseeds to Pacific ports since early January.
The effect has been a severe backlog of vessels on the Pacific coast and more than C$15 million in demurrage fines levied against the CWB.
Thirty two ships waited to load at Canada's Pacific ports with one ship berthed as long as 49 days as of Friday.

Manitoba elevators had the least space available at 14 percent, unchanged from the week before, Saskatchewan was next at 17 percent, down from 18 percent the prior week, and Alberta had the most vacancy at 21 percent, unchanged from the week before.
Vancouver saw 3,121 railcars unloaded compared to the target of 3,400 hopper cars. The prior week saw 3,433 unloads.
Prince Rupert unloads totalled 1,213 railcars compared to the target of 1,500 hopper cars. Last week saw 1,299 unloads.
Thunder Bay saw 621 railcar unloads compared to the target of 850 hopper cars. The prior week saw 1,138 unloads.
